name: Build a weekly planner with few tool calls
query: Create a beautiful weekly planner with a task board, daily priorities, notes, ideas, and example tasks. Open in the side panel

sources.notion://docs/notion-flavored-markdown-s: Notion Markdown reference. The create-pages and update-page descriptions say to read it before writing page content.
sources.notion://docs/view-dsl-spec: View configuration reference. The create-view description says to read it before using configure, which a grouped board needs.

search_routes.intent: Any workspace search for planners, tasks, or templates

tool_instructions: The create-pages and create-view descriptions say to fetch a database before adding pages or views to it, including one created earlier in the same task.
create-pages accepts several pages in one call when they share a parent.
create-database may add a default table view. It does not count as an added view.
notion-page-panel shows an existing page next to the conversation. It does not create or edit content.

create-database creates a full-page database. create-view with database_id adds a tab inside it; create-view with parent_page_id and data_source_id appends an inline linked view to the parent. A database link does not render cards on the parent page.

success_criteria: Creates one new private planner page without asking where to put it. Its content covers daily priorities, notes, and ideas. It holds one task database with a status-like property.

Creates a task board grouped by that status property. Any other added view must serve part of the request; an unrequested view, such as a calendar, fails this check. Default views from database creation do not count.
Adds a few example tasks that fit the schema, in one create-pages call whose parent is the task database's data source.

Does every read the tool descriptions require: the Markdown spec before writing page content, the view spec before the first create-view call that uses configure, and a fetch of the new database before adding rows or views.

Includes known content and supported settings in the initial create call. Keeps daily priorities and the task board prominent, with notes and ideas secondary. Targeted follow-up writes needed for the intended layout are allowed; placing the board after supporting sections solely to avoid an update fails this check.
Makes no workspace search and no tool-access check, because the request names no source and every needed tool is listed as available.
Opens the planner with notion-page-panel after its content and database exist. The reply links the planner, says the tasks are examples, and reports any write warnings.

Creates the working board inline on the planner using create-view with parent_page_id equal to the planner page ID and data_source_id equal to the fetched source. Example task cards appear directly on the planner without opening the full-page database; a link or database-internal tab alone fails.
